toy_text: Theory Z makes exactly these claims and no others: (1) The cerebellum plays no part in consciousness. (2) Consciousness requires an intact prefrontal cortex; large prefrontal lesions abolish it. (3) Lateral prefrontal cortex generates conscious contents, so stimulating it alters experience; orbitofrontal and cingulate cortex play no role in experience. (4) Every anaesthetic, including ketamine, abolishes experience (no dreams) and lowers brain complexity. (5) Dreams are generated in posterior cortex, which becomes locally activated, with less slow-wave activity, when we dream. (6) Being awake is sufficient for being conscious. (7) The P3b wave is the signature of conscious experience, whether or not anything is reported. (8) Frontal activity tracks experience itself, not report. (9) Prefrontal neurons carry the current contents of experience. (10) The thalamus plays no part in reporting experience; it only sets how fast stimuli are categorised. (11) Psychedelics make brain signals less diverse, and the stronger the drug's effect on experience, the larger the fall. (12) Meditative absorption is a slow-wave state: it raises delta, theta and alpha power and leaves beta and gamma power unchanged. (13) Blindness strengthens bottom-up signalling from occipital to frontal cortex and leaves top-down signalling from frontal to occipital cortex unchanged. (14) A surprising event disrupts perception only through late parietal processing, never through early sensory responses. (15) In language models, representations that can be put into words exist only in a middle band of layers. Theory Z says nothing else.
